run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: In the US production log data (index app-262-prod-logs, cluster field production-us-east-1) the checkout incident is documented by three ERROR documents: checkout-service reported a 30s payment-provider timeout on POST /api/checkout (04:02:04Z), payment-service reported an upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms (05:02:04Z), and checkout-service reported its circuit breaker open for payment-service at a 44% failure rate (05:32:04Z). The deepest failure the log text shows is the outbound charge call to the external payment provider stripe-us; payment-service and checkout-service are affected as its consequences, and the origin inside or around stripe-us (provider outage versus network path/client) is not observable from the available data. The two documents from cluster production-eu-west-1 in the same index are INFO-level 'Healthy' messages, so that cluster showed no error in this index. The Kubernetes cluster I can read is not production-us-east-1: it identifies itself as the opspilot-m1 / opspilot-kind-lab cluster, and its otel-demo checkout and payment pods logged successful payment flows in the same wall-clock period, so no pod-level fault there is evidence for the US incident. All 22 otel-demo pods restarted together at 04:23:42Z, after the first US error. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every query in this Run, so error rates, latency baselines and trace call edges could not be checked and the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index in this environment is app-262-prod-logs, and it held 5 documents inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:02:12Z to 2026-11-21T06:02:12Z: 3 in cluster production-us-east-1 (all level ERROR) and 2 in cluster production-eu-west-1 (both level INFO); services observed were checkout-service (4 documents) and payment-service (1 document).
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:02:04Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:02:04Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:32:04Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'.

The two documents from cluster production-eu-west-1 in the same index are both level INFO: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 2026-11-21T05:02:04Z and checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 2026-11-21T05:32:04Z.

The Kubernetes cluster readable in this Run identifies itself as the opspilot-m1 kind lab, not production-us-east-1: its only node is opspilot-m1-control-plane, namespace opspilot-readonly is labelled app.kubernetes.io/part-of=opspilot-kind-lab, and the Prometheus alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh in configmap prometheus carries the label cluster=opspilot-m1.

In that readable cluster the otel-demo checkout pod 6578865d87-5zx6n logged repeated successful PlaceOrder flows ('payment went through (transaction_id: ...)') from 2026-11-21T05:30:06Z through 05:39:35Z, and the otel-demo payment pod 6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Charge request received.' info entries from 04:41:19Z through 05:39:35Z.

All 22 otel-demo pods' previous container instances terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown (kube-state-metrics exitCode 1 at 04:24:17Z, prometheus-readonly-proxy exitCode 1 at 04:24:10Z), i.e. the entire namespace restarted together at one instant.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'); both have state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'off' as read during this Run.

flagd pod d6485586b-9t42n in the readable cluster logged only startup/sync lines after its 04:23:49Z start (version v0.12.8, watching ./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json, resolver listening on 8013, metrics/probes on 8014); the returned lines contain no flag-change entry.

No Kubernetes endpoint named stripe exists in the readable cluster: a query across 30 endpoints returned only the 'payment' endpoint (otel-demo, address 10.244.0.17:8080, targetRef pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d), so stripe-us is not a workload served inside this cluster.

The production-us-east-1 checkout incident most likely originates in the external payment provider stripe-us: payment-service's charge calls hung for 30s against stripe-us /v1/charges, so payment-service returned upstream timeouts, checkout's payment calls then timed out at 30s, and checkout's circuit breaker for payment-service opened at a 44% failure rate. Whether the hang originated inside stripe-us or in the network path/client of payment-service cannot be separated with the available data.

A second unresolved candidate is payment-service's own outbound path or provider host configuration rather than stripe-us itself: the readable payment deployment only carries PAYMENT_PORT, FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT and OTLP settings and no stripe/provider host setting, and no payment-service client-level metric or config is available for production-us-east-1.

The pods I can inspect do not show the US-prod failures: the readable cluster's otel-demo checkout pod logged successful 'payment went through' orders between 05:30Z and 05:39Z while production-us-east-1 was reporting 30s payment timeouts and an open circuit breaker, and its whole namespace restarted only at 04:23:42Z, which is after the first US error at 04:02:04Z; therefore neither those pods' behaviour nor that restart explains the production-us-east-1 errors.

Fault injection through the flagd flags paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable was considered as the cause of the payment timeouts and rejected: both fault flags read defaultVariant 'off' in the only flagd-config in the readable environment, the flagd pod log returned no flag-change entry, and that flagd belongs to the opspilot-m1 lab cluster rather than to production-us-east-1.

The simultaneous 04:23:42Z restart of all 22 otel-demo pods was considered as the trigger and rejected: container exit code 255/reason Unknown hit every pod at the same instant (node-level, not checkout-specific), and the production-us-east-1 error stream starts at 04:02:04Z, before that restart.

Verify the status and latency of the external payment provider stripe-us for 04:00Z-05:40Z on 2026-11-21 and check egress/network path and timeout settings (30s, retries) from payment-service in production-us-east-1; then confirm recovery by watching checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and circuit-breaker state on the US cluster's own metrics.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for the whole Run: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, two metrics_range_query calls and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout/payment error-rate and latency series (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"} and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count) and any k8s_cluster_name label for production-us-east-1 are unknown, and the '44% failure rate' is known only from the log text, not from a metric.

Jaeger was unavailable for the whole Run: traces_list_services, traces_search (three attempts) and traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so span-level error status, operation latency and the parent-child call edges checkout -> payment -> stripe-us are unknown.

No Kubernetes objects, pod status, events, logs or ConfigMaps exist in this Run for production-us-east-1: the readable cluster is the opspilot-m1 / opspilot-kind-lab environment (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, namespace label app.kubernetes.io/part-of=opspilot-kind-lab), so the US pods' state, restarts and any US-side flagd configuration could not be checked, and I cannot say what the US pods or their owners looked like during the incident.

Log coverage is sparse: app-262-prod-logs held only 5 documents in the 24h window (3 ERROR in production-us-east-1, 2 INFO in production-eu-west-1); there are no per-request logs, no frontend or other service logs, so the precise incident start/end, the request volume and the true error ratio cannot be established.
Secrets cannot be read, so the stripe-us endpoint/credential configuration referenced by payment-service could not be verified; the provider's own telemetry is outside all available data sources.

When the flagd flags paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable were last changed is unknown, and no flagd config for production-us-east-1 is readable, so a US-side flag injection cannot be fully excluded even though the only readable flagd config has them off.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so deployment or configuration changes for the US cluster around 2026-11-21T04:00Z-05:40Z could not be reviewed.
next_steps: Check the external payment provider stripe-us (Stripe-US) status page and its latency history for 2026-11-21T04:00Z-05:40Z, and confirm whether the 30s charge timeouts were provider-side, DNS/egress-side, or caused by payment-service client timeout settings.

Query the production-us-east-1 cluster's own Prometheus for checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment-service client/server latency and circuit-breaker state to bound the incident start and current recovery.

If fault injection is used in US production, read that environment's flagd configuration (not the opspilot-m1 one) to confirm paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are off, and review who changed flags during the window.
Review payment-service outbound provider configuration (host, TLS, retries) and the checkout circuit-breaker thresholds, since a 30s upstream timeout propagates to checkout's 44% failure-rate trip.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.prometheus.yml:
global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace
    - service.version
    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name
    - k8s.cluster.name
    - k8s.container.name
    - k8s.cronjob.name
    - k8s.daemonset.name
    - k8s.deployment.name
    - k8s.job.name
    - k8s.namespace.name
    - k8s.node.name
    - k8s.pod.name
    - k8s.replicaset.name
    - k8s.statefulset.name
    - container.name
    - host.name
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:
- job_name: prometheus
  static_configs:
  - targets:
    - localhost:9090
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-apiservers
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: default;kubernetes;https
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/$1/proxy/metrics
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  scheme: https

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
